title: Conventional Commits encourages focus on the wrong things
summary: This article argues that Conventional Commits specification, while well-intentioned, misdirects developer focus toward machine-parseable commit messages instead of meaningful code review and collaboration, suggesting the emphasis on automated changelog generation distracts from more important engineering practices.
problem_solved: Addresses the question of whether Conventional Commits adds real value or just creates overhead by prioritizing machine-readability over human communication.
why_valuable: Provides a critical perspective on a widely-adopted convention, encouraging developers to question blindly-followed practices and focus on what actually improves software quality.
